question: Not shared. P-307 identifies MCI present at the assessment (Petersen/IWG criteria with MoCA < 26, confirmed by a senior neurologist) in older inpatients with chronic pain (aged >= 60, one pain department in Nanchang). P-165 predicts MCI onset, that is whether a recorded MCI diagnosis code appears within one year after a primary-care visit, for every visit by a patient aged >= 65 in Stanford Healthcare's EHR. Data after the visit are masked. One task is diagnosis of current status in a comorbidity-defined inpatient group; the other is one-year prognosis of a billing diagnosis in unselected primary care. The comparison therefore differs (prevalent MCI against non-MCI, or future coded MCI against none), and so does the population (chronic-pain inpatients against all older primary-care patients). The broad channel (clinical/questionnaire/EHR data) is shared, and the predictor sets differ (7 pain, mood, sleep and demographic variables against 480 EHR and clinical-note concepts), which condition 1 would allow.

figures.P-307: XGBoost test-set AUC 0.925, printed 95% CI 0.863-0.995 (random 30% test set, n = 184; overall MCI prevalence 169/612 = 27.6%). Logistic regression test AUC 0.895 (0.829-0.966).
figures.P-165: Random forest test ROC-AUC 68.2 +/- 0.7 (%), temporal split (train on visits up to 2019, test on visits from 2020 on). XGBoost 66.8 +/- 0.8, logistic regression 57.0 +/- 1.1. Taking +/- 0.7 as one standard error gives a 95% interval of about [0.668, 0.696]. The test-set size is not printed. The whole cohort has 531,387 visits, so any interval derived from the test set would be narrow.

matched_figure_check: No matched figure exists. P-165 reports no cross-sectional identification of current MCI and no result in a pain population. P-307 reports no incident or one-year-ahead result and no result in a general primary-care population.
performance_validity: Exclusion does not apply. P-307's 0.925 is below 0.97 (its upper CI bound is 0.995), on an internal random 30% test set of 184 patients, with SMOTETomek applied to the training set only. P-165 uses a large temporal hold-out.
reason: The two studies ask different clinical questions. P-307 identifies MCI present at a research-criteria work-up in older chronic-pain inpatients. P-165 predicts whether an MCI diagnosis code will be recorded within the next year for any older primary-care patient, using only data up to the visit (condition 1: the task and the population differ). The AUCs (0.925, CI 0.863-0.995, against 0.682 +/- 0.007) would otherwise differ beyond uncertainty.

quotes.quote: The outcome of this study was the occurrence of MCI, which was diagnosed according to Petersen’s Criteria and the International Working Group on MCI
In this study, 612 older patients with chronic pain were recruited from the Pain Department of a tertiary general hospital in Nanchang, China
the XGBoost model performed best, achieving an accuracy of 0.883 and an AUC of 0.925 (95% CI 0.863–0.995).
develop machine learning models to predict MCI up to a year in advance of recorded diagnosis
We train our machine learning models to predict onset of MCI within one year of patients’ visits with their primary care provider for patients 65 years or older.
Note, data after the primary care visit time were masked and not used to perform the prediction.
The random forest model has a higher ROC-AUC (68.2%±0.7%) than xgboost and logistic regression models on the test set.
